claims.claim: Terminology: IDPC 'Dealer Member' excludes mutual fund dealer members (i.e. the Investment Dealer)
claims.quote: except, for the purposes of these Rules, Mutual Fund Dealer Members are to be excluded.

claims.claim: Approved Person = individual approved by CIRO to carry out a function for a Dealer Member
claims.quote: An individual approved by the Corporation under these Rules to carry out a function for a Dealer Member

claims.claim: Approved Person list includes Registered Representative
claims.quote: (viii) Registered Representative,

claims.claim: Registered Representative definition
claims.quote: An individual, approved by the Corporation, to trade, or advise on trades, in securities or derivatives with the public in Canada, on the Dealer Member's behalf

claims.claim: Rationale for relationship disclosure (IDPC 3216): clients should understand the services they will receive when opening an account (attributed to s.3216, not the CRM as a whole)
claims.quote: all clients should have a good understanding of the services they will be provided when they open an account

claims.claim: CRM project addressed four elements: relationship disclosure, conflicts management/disclosure, suitability assessment, account performance reporting
claims.quote: Relationship disclosure; Conflicts of interest management/disclosure; Suitability assessment; and Account performance reporting.

claims.claim: The CRM elements are designed to work together
claims.quote: the intent of the CRM project was for the different elements to work together within the larger CRM framework

claims.claim: Agency vs principal: for listed equities the dealer usually acts as agent for a commission; for bonds and other OTC products it usually acts as principal, selling from inventory at a markup or spread
claims.basis: standard industry concept (agency vs principal trading; equities typically agency/commission, OTC fixed income typically principal/markup or spread); no corpus text, C by design

claims.claim: Trust: client relies on the RR's competence and honesty; this reliance helps explain the KYC, suitability and conflict duties (framed as the guide's explanation, labelled concept)
claims.basis: standard concept; descriptive only, no statement of a legal standard of care (source map caveat 5)

claims.claim: Firm must take reasonable steps to identify material conflicts between firm/Approved Person and client
claims.quote: A Dealer Member must take reasonable steps to identify existing material conflicts of interest, and material conflicts of interest that are reasonably foreseeable

claims.claim: Dealer must be registered or exempt in each jurisdiction where its clients reside (Key rule)
claims.quote: registered (or exempt from such registration) in the appropriate category under securities laws in each jurisdiction in which clients of the Dealer Member reside

claims.claim: Same registration requirement for the individual
claims.quote: the individual, if required to do so under securities laws, is registered (or exempt from such registration) in the appropriate category under securities laws in each jurisdiction in which clients of the individual reside

claims.claim: Dealing with a client located in another country (U.S. resident or snowbird abroad) can engage that country's securities rules, which are outside the exam's sources; follow firm cross-border policy and involve compliance
claims.basis: hedged practice statement only; does not assert what foreign law requires (gap G1, 02b-gap-fill-instruments: keep U.S.-law content conceptual). IDPC 2551(1) is the only R claim on this point

claims.claim: Individual mobility exemption: 5 or fewer eligible clients in the local jurisdiction
claims.quote: the individual does not act as a dealer, underwriter or adviser in the local jurisdiction other than for 5 or fewer eligible clients

claims.claim: Firm mobility exemption: 10 or fewer eligible clients
claims.quote: the person or company does not act as a dealer, underwriter or adviser in the local jurisdiction other than in respect of 10 or fewer eligible clients

claims.claim: Eligible client = client immediately before becoming resident in the local jurisdiction
claims.quote: the client is an individual and was a client of the person or company immediately before becoming resident in the local jurisdiction

claims.claim: Eligible client includes spouse or child of such a client
claims.quote: the client is the spouse or a child of a client referred to in paragraph (a)

claims.claim: Firm must disclose the exemption to the client before first acting
claims.quote: before first acting as a dealer or adviser for an eligible client, the individual’s sponsoring firm has disclosed to the client that the individual

claims.claim: Mobility condition: individual registered in principal jurisdiction
claims.quote: the individual is registered as a dealing, advising or associate advising representative in the individual’s principal jurisdiction

claims.claim: Mobility condition: sponsoring firm registered
claims.quote: the individual’s sponsoring firm is registered in the firm’s principal jurisdiction

claims.claim: Mobility condition: individual complies with Part 13
claims.quote: the individual complies with Part 13 Dealing with clients

claims.claim: Disclosure before first acting: individual not subject to local requirements
claims.quote: is not subject to requirements otherwise applicable under local securities legislation

claims.claim: Sponsoring firm files Form 31-103F3 as soon as possible after the individual first relies on the exemption
claims.quote: the individual’s sponsoring firm must submit a completed Form 31-103F3 Use of Mobility Exemption to the securities regulatory authority of the local jurisdiction as soon as possible after the individual first relies on this section

claims.claim: Exemption is triggered when the client moves, not the registrant (Exam trap)
claims.quote: The exemption becomes available when the client (not the registrant) moves to another jurisdiction.

claims.claim: Departure tax: emigrant deemed to have disposed of certain property at FMV
claims.locator: CRA 'Dispositions of property for emigrants' / Departure tax, ~L78
claims.quote: you are considered to have sold certain types of property (even if you have not sold them) at their fair market value (FMV) and to have immediately reacquired them for the same amount

claims.claim: Registered plans and pensions excluded from deemed disposition
claims.locator: CRA emigrant pages, exceptions to deemed disposition, ~L242
claims.quote: pension plans, annuities, registered retirement savings plans, pooled registered pension plans, registered retirement income funds, registered education savings plans, registered disability savings plans, tax-free savings accounts

claims.claim: Emigrant may keep the TFSA and continue to benefit from the exemption on investment income and withdrawals
claims.quote: If you hold a TFSA when you leave Canada, you can keep it and continue to benefit from the exemption from Canadian tax on investment income and withdrawals

claims.claim: Non-resident TFSA withdrawals remain tax-free
claims.quote: You may withdraw money from your TFSA tax-free if you become a non-resident.

claims.claim: Non-resident contributions taxed at 1% per month until withdrawn or resident again
claims.locator: CRA TFSA non-resident page, 'How non-resident contributions are taxed', ~L1690
claims.quote: Any non-resident contribution you make, except for a qualifying transfer or an exempt contribution, is subject to a 1% tax for each month the contribution remains in the account.

claims.claim: 1% tax continues until withdrawal or return to residency
claims.quote: This tax continues to apply until you withdraw the non-resident contribution or you become a resident of Canada again.

claims.claim: RRSP withdrawals by non-residents: 25% withholding unless reduced by treaty
claims.quote: For non-residents of Canada, withholding is 25% unless reduced by a treaty.

claims.claim: Each CRM requirement is part of the broader obligation to deal fairly, honestly and in good faith with clients
claims.quote: each of these requirements is a part of the broader fundamental obligation of the Dealer and its representatives under securities legislation to deal fairly, honestly and in good faith with clients

claims.claim: Mobility exemption client limits apply in each other jurisdiction
claims.locator: 31-103CP s.2.2 Limits on the number of clients, ~L82
claims.quote: The limits in sections 2.2 and 8.30 are per jurisdiction.

claims.claim: Mobility condition: individual acts fairly, honestly and in good faith with the eligible client
claims.quote: they act fairly, honestly and in good faith in their dealings with the eligible client

claims.claim: Firm supervises individuals who rely on the mobility exemption
claims.quote: The registered firm must have appropriate policies and procedures for supervising individuals who rely on a mobility

claims.claim: Firm keeps records showing compliance with mobility exemption conditions
claims.quote: Registered firms must also keep appropriate records to demonstrate they are complying with the conditions of the mobility

claims.claim: Emigrant must notify Canadian payers and financial institutions of non-resident status
claims.locator: CRA 'Leaving Canada (emigrants)' - What you need to do, ~L46
claims.quote: you are required to notify any Canadian payers and your financial institutions that you are no longer a resident of Canada

claims.claim: Intuition: registration where clients reside lets the client's regulator have authority over the firm that serves the client
claims.basis: Plain-language rationale for IDPC 2551(1); labelled 'The intuition'; no rule claim

claims.claim: Principal trades put the firm on the other side of the client's trade; client usually cannot check advice
claims.basis: Standard agency/principal concept; non-normative

claims.claim: Scenario Astrid Lunde: ON client (an individual) retires to BC; RR has 3 eligible clients there, 4th within limit of 5; firm registered in BC (else firm exemption, 10 or fewer); disclosure before first acting, F3 as soon as possible; retirement (income/horizon) is the significant KYC change
claims.basis: Applies NI 31-103 ss.1.1, 2.2(1)(a)-(g), 8.30; IDPC 2551(1); GN-3400 s.2.11.2 significant change; 3+1=4 <= 5. Revised fix round 1 (F02, F03, F04).

claims.claim: Firm must learn and remain informed of essential facts about every order, account and client
claims.quote: learn and remain informed of the essential facts relative to every order, account and client it accepts

claims.claim: Establish identity; inquire into reputation if cause for concern
claims.quote: establish the identity of a client and, if the Dealer Member has any cause for concern, make reasonable inquiries as to the reputation of the client

claims.claim: Establish insider status
claims.quote: establish whether the client is an insider of a reporting issuer or any other issuer whose securities are publicly traded

claims.claim: The six KYC factors (quote is from the RDI suitability description in 3216(5)(ii)(d)(I), which lists the same six factors as 3202(1)(iii)(a))
claims.quote: the client’s personal and financial circumstances, investment needs and objectives, investment time horizon, risk profile and investment knowledge

claims.claim: 3202(1)(iii): collect sufficient information on the listed factors to meet Rule 3400 obligations
claims.quote: ensure it has collected sufficient information regarding all of the following to enable it to meet its obligations under Rule 3400

claims.claim: Establish creditworthiness if financing the client's purchase
claims.quote: establish the creditworthiness of the client if the Dealer Member is financing the client’s acquisition of a security

claims.claim: Personal circumstances content
claims.quote: civil status or family situation, number of dependants, employment status and the details of their current or former occupation

claims.claim: Financial circumstances content incl. liquidity needs, net worth, borrowing
claims.quote: annual income, liquidity needs, financial assets, net worth, and whether the client is using leverage or borrowing to finance the purchase of securities

claims.claim: Net worth includes assets and liabilities
claims.quote: A Dealer should also take reasonable steps to determine a client’s net worth, which includes their assets and liabilities.

claims.claim: Investment objectives examples
claims.quote: A client’s investment objectives are what they want to achieve when investing, such as capital preservation, income generation, capital growth, or investing in accordance with their personal values.

claims.claim: Investment knowledge content
claims.quote: the financial markets, the relative risk and limitations of various types of investments, and how the level of risk taken affects potential returns

claims.claim: Time horizon assessed for feasibility
claims.quote: the Dealer has the responsibility to assess its feasibility and reasonableness relative to the client’s liquidity needs, age, investment objectives, risk profile, and other particular circumstances

claims.claim: Liquidity needs assessment
claims.quote: a Registered Individual should consider whether the client has other means to cover their expenditures, whether the needs are expected or unexpected, and whether, once the need materializes, the money will be withdrawn on a regular basis

claims.claim: Borrowing to invest: gather info on ability to meet debt obligations
claims.quote: When a client uses leverage or borrows money to invest, the Dealer should gather information on the client’s ability to meet debt obligations.

claims.claim: ESG criteria and personal preferences recognized
claims.quote: investing in accordance with environmental, social and governance criteria or other personal preferences

claims.claim: EDI considerations recorded as a client preference/restriction (e.g. favouring issuers with diverse boards)
claims.basis: syllabus wording only; no corpus text names EDI (gap G3)

claims.claim: KYC must not be manipulated to match a product or reach a pre-determined outcome (Exam trap)
claims.quote: Dealers and Registered Individuals must not manipulate KYC information to correspond or match with a security, account, portfolio or otherwise be manipulated to lead to a pre-determined outcome.

claims.claim: KYC also collected as gatekeepers incl. AML
claims.quote: Dealers are also required to collect KYC information as part of their role as gatekeepers of our financial markets, including complying with their anti-money laundering (AML) regulatory obligations

claims.claim: Without adequate and timely KYC the firm cannot meet suitability obligations (used in 1.2 and 1.7)
claims.quote: Without adequate and timely KYC information, a Dealer cannot meet their suitability determination obligations and other regulatory obligations.

claims.claim: KYC specific to each client; do not attribute spouse's knowledge
claims.quote: should not attribute characteristics of the client’s family members to the client, such as attributing a spouse’s investment experience and knowledge.

claims.claim: Insider status: explain what an insider is, then ask
claims.quote: Dealers should explain to the client what an insider is and what it means for securities to be publicly traded and then ask the client whether they are an insider.

claims.claim: RR may need to ask about assets and liabilities held outside the firm
claims.quote: A Registered Individual may need to ask about investments, other assets and liabilities the client maintains outside the Dealer

claims.claim: Entity personal circumstances: constating documents
claims.quote: form and details regarding the organization of the legal entity, i.e. articles of incorporation, trust deed, or other constating documents

claims.claim: Entity personal circumstances: persons authorized to instruct and limits on authority
claims.quote: persons authorized to provide instructions on the account and details of any restrictions on their authority

claims.claim: Inconsistent knowledge answers: make further inquiries
claims.quote: Registered Individuals should always make further inquiries if the information provided by a client appears to be inconsistent with their apparent level of investment knowledge.

claims.claim: Example: limited knowledge but willing to take high risk
claims.quote: a client may indicate that they have limited investment knowledge and experience, while also indicating a willingness to take on a high level of risk

claims.claim: Clients express objectives in meaningful terms
claims.quote: Dealers should provide their clients with the opportunity to express their investment needs and objectives in terms that are meaningful to them

claims.claim: Objective examples: retirement lifestyle, home purchase
claims.quote: saving for retirement to maintain a certain lifestyle

claims.claim: Short horizon may mean only conservative investments suitable
claims.quote: a short investment time horizon may mean that conservative investments may be the only suitable option

claims.claim: Do not pre-populate KYC questionnaires before interacting (exam trap)
claims.quote: pre-populate questionnaires with the KYC information required under clause 3202(1)(iii) before interacting with the client

claims.claim: Do not combine multiple KYC variables in one question (exam trap)
claims.quote: combine multiple KYC variables into one question

claims.claim: Loan stays due when securities fall (supports 'leverage magnifies losses')
claims.quote: your responsibility to repay the loan and pay interest as required by its terms remains the same even if the value of the securities purchased declines

claims.claim: Risk profile = willingness (tolerance) and ability (capacity)
claims.quote: willingness to accept risk, sometimes referred to as risk tolerance, and ability to endure financial loss, sometimes referred to as risk capacity

claims.claim: Risk profile reflects the lower of tolerance and capacity (Key rule)
claims.quote: The client’s risk profile should reflect the lower of the client’s assessed risk tolerance and risk capacity.

claims.claim: Risk capacity factors: share of total investments; age and life stage
claims.quote: how much of a client’s total investments an account or a particular securities position represents

claims.claim: Risk capacity factor: age and life stage
claims.quote: the client’s age and life stage

claims.claim: Behavioural influences on tolerance (loss aversion, overconfidence, recency, framing); capacity also reflects current holdings, horizon, liquidity (syllabus)
claims.basis: standard behavioural-finance concepts; syllabus 1.3 parameters

claims.claim: Risk need: required return, market environment, consequence of failure; never lifts profile above lower of tolerance/capacity
claims.basis: standard planning concept; no regulatory text uses 'risk need' (source map 1.3, caveat 5); cap consistent with GN-KYC lower-of rule

claims.claim: Thorough process: interpret responses without inappropriate weight
claims.quote: appropriately interpreting client responses to questions and not attributing inappropriate weight to certain answers

claims.claim: Identify clients better suited to cash deposits or guaranteed products
claims.quote: identifying clients that are more suited to placing their money in cash deposits or guaranteed products because they are unwilling or unable to accept the risk of loss of capital

claims.claim: Questions and answers documented
claims.quote: The questions and answers that are used to establish the level of risk a client is willing and able to take should be documented.

claims.claim: Resolving conflicts: discuss risk and return
claims.quote: the Registered Individual should consider having a detailed discussion with the client on the relationship between risk and return

claims.claim: Never override the risk profile to meet return expectations
claims.quote: Registered Individuals should not override a client’s risk profile or other KYC information to meet a client’s expectations for returns.

claims.claim: Resolving conflicts: identify mismatches between needs/objectives, tolerance and capacity and revisit with client (list aligned item for item with 7.5, X16)
claims.quote: The Registered Individual should identify any mismatches between the client’s investment needs and objectives, risk tolerance and risk capacity and revisit them with the client.

claims.claim: Explain alternatives
claims.quote: the Registered Individual should clearly explain the alternatives available

claims.claim: Explain higher-risk portfolio is unsuitable; document interaction and result
claims.quote: The Registered Individual should properly document their interaction with the client and the end result.

claims.claim: Higher risk portfolio unsuitable where capacity/tolerance lacking
claims.quote: their need or expectation for a higher return cannot realistically be met, and as a result, the higher risk portfolio is unsuitable

claims.claim: Exam trap: eager 68-year-old with retirement-dependent savings: high tolerance, low capacity, low profile
claims.basis: application of the lower-of rule

claims.claim: Tolerance and capacity separate considerations that together make up the risk profile
claims.quote: Risk tolerance and risk capacity are separate considerations that together make up the client’s overall risk profile.

claims.claim: RR should consider setting out return assumptions required by objectives (risk need link)
claims.quote: A Registered Individual should consider setting out investment return assumptions required to meet the client’s investment needs and objectives.

claims.claim: Thorough process: check products in account fit tolerance and capacity
claims.quote: determining whether the products and services the client has access to within their account are appropriate for them based on their assessed risk tolerance and risk capacity

claims.claim: Risk questions fair, clear, not misleading
claims.quote: The questions should be fair, clear and not misleading.

claims.claim: RR must not influence client's answers to risk questions
claims.quote: clients should not be influenced by a Registered Individual as to the way they respond to questions related to their risk tolerance or risk capacity

claims.claim: Why the lower of tolerance and capacity: panic selling (tolerance failure) or damage to essential goal (capacity failure)
claims.basis: Standard risk-profiling rationale; consistent with GN-3400 s.2.3.5 'lower of' rule

claims.claim: Tolerance can be overstated after rises/understated after falls; check against knowledge and past behaviour
claims.basis: Standard behavioural-finance concept (recency, framing); see 7.3

claims.claim: Scenario Tomasz Wierzbicki: stated high tolerance contradicted by past selling; low capacity; profile low; 9% target is risk need
claims.basis: Applies GN-3400 s.2.3.5 lower-of rule and resolution steps (existing claims 57-61)

claims.claim: Sole proprietorship definition
claims.quote: An unincorporated business entirely owned by one person.

claims.claim: Partnership definition
claims.quote: An association or relationship between two or more individuals, corporations, trusts or partnerships that join together to carry on a trade or business.

claims.claim: Partnership profits/losses usually divided per partnership agreement
claims.quote: The business profits (or losses) are usually divided among the partners based on the partnership agreement.

claims.claim: Unlimited liability of sole proprietor and general partners; limited partners' liability limited to investment; sole prop business needs feed owner's KYC
claims.basis: standard business-law concept

claims.claim: Corporation: limited liability
claims.quote: Shareholders are not responsible for a corporation's debts.

claims.claim: Corporation: continuous existence
claims.quote: Corporations live on until they wind up, amalgamate, or give up their charter

claims.claim: Corporation: taxed separately
claims.locator: ISED 'Benefits of incorporating' - Lower tax rates, ~L110
claims.quote: Corporations are taxed separately from their owners. Corporate tax rates are generally lower than personal income tax rates.

claims.claim: Corporation: can raise money by selling shares or bonds
claims.locator: ISED 'Benefits of incorporating' - Easier access to capital, ~L106
claims.quote: They can also raise money by selling shares or bonds to investors

claims.claim: Public corporation: shares listed on designated Canadian exchange
claims.quote: it has a class of shares listed on a designated Canadian stock exchange

claims.quote: no class of its shares of capital stock is listed on a designated stock exchange

claims.claim: CCPC not controlled by non-residents

claims.claim: Co-operative: member-based model
claims.quote: Learn about co-operatives, their member-based model, types and financial structure

claims.quote: Create a cooperative under the Canada Cooperatives Act by filing an application with Corporations Canada.

claims.claim: Co-operatives may alternatively be incorporated under provincial co-operatives legislation

claims.claim: Co-op democratic control, one member one vote, surplus to members; member shares illiquid; investment authority from by-laws/board
claims.basis: standard co-operative concept (no corpus text, gap noted)

claims.claim: Partnership account: establish existence and business
claims.quote: establish the existence of the partnership or trust and the nature of its business

claims.claim: Partnership account: identify controlling individuals
claims.quote: establish the identity of each individual that exercises control over the affairs of the partnership or trust

claims.claim: Corporate account: directors' names within 30 days
claims.quote: obtain the names of all directors of the corporation within 30 days of opening the account

claims.claim: Corporate account: identify holders of 25% or more of voting rights
claims.quote: 25% or more of the voting rights attached to the outstanding voting securities

claims.claim: Corporate account needs its own application with the corporation's info
claims.quote: a Dealer cannot use the same account application to open a corporate account, as the corporate account’s owner is the corporation and not the corporation’s beneficial owner

claims.claim: Owners/directors of public companies may be insiders with trading restrictions
claims.basis: standard concept; insider status collected under IDPC 3202(1)(ii)

claims.claim: CIPF generally treats a corporation or partnership as separate from its owners
claims.locator: CIPF coverage page - Limits for Corporations, Partnerships, ~L61
claims.quote: is generally considered to be separate from its owners or partners for purposes of determining the limit on CIPF protection

claims.claim: CIPF exceptions for certain personal holding corporations, partnerships and unincorporated organizations
claims.locator: CIPF coverage page - Limits for Corporations, Partnerships, ~L63
claims.quote: There are exceptions to this general rule for certain types of personal holding corporations, partnerships and unincorporated organizations

claims.claim: Business ends when owner dies for non-corporate structures
claims.quote: With other business structures, a business stops existing when the owner dies.

claims.claim: Corporate tax rates generally lower than personal rates
claims.locator: ISED 'Benefits of incorporating' - Lower tax rates, ~L68
claims.quote: Corporate tax rates are generally lower than personal income tax rates.

claims.claim: Corporation's beneficial owners are separate persons from the corporation (scenario)
claims.quote: The beneficial owner(s) of a corporation are separate and distinct persons from the corporate legal entity.

claims.claim: Why structure matters (whose money, who instructs, who controls); lower corporate tax lets more profit stay invested
claims.basis: Inference from ISED tax statement and IDPC 3203/3204; labelled concept

claims.claim: Firm must take reasonable steps to have client confirm accuracy of KYC
claims.quote: take reasonable steps to have a client confirm the accuracy of such information

claims.claim: Evidence by signature or file notes
claims.quote: Dealers may evidence this confirmation by obtaining the client’s signature (handwritten, electronic or digital signature), or by maintaining notes in the client file detailing any client instructions to change the information.

claims.claim: Verify changes in writing and allow correction
claims.quote: Dealers should verify any change to client information by confirming it with the client in writing and providing the client with an opportunity to correct any changes.

claims.claim: Record date of collection
claims.quote: Dealers should record the date on which information is collected under subsection 3202(1)

claims.claim: Keep evidence of confirmation
claims.quote: Dealers should maintain evidence of the client’s confirmation of the accuracy of their KYC information.

claims.claim: Records must document correspondence with clients
claims.quote: document correspondence with clients

claims.claim: Records demonstrate compliance with KYC/appropriateness/PDD/KYP/suitability
claims.quote: account appropriateness, product due diligence, know-your-product and suitability determination requirements

claims.claim: Extra controls for name, address or banking changes (fraud risk)
claims.quote: Dealers should consider implementing additional controls for changes in client name, address or banking information or other areas where there is an increased risk of fraud.

claims.claim: RR documents disclosure of material positive and negative factors
claims.quote: We expect the Registered Individual to document this disclosure.

claims.claim: Why documentation matters: client can check understanding; firm can show compliance
claims.basis: Plain-language rationale; non-normative

claims.claim: TCP definition
claims.quote: means an individual identified by a client to a Dealer Member or Approved Person whom the Dealer Member or Approved Person may contact in accordance with the client’s written consent

claims.claim: Vulnerable client definition
claims.quote: means a client who might have an illness, impairment, disability or aging-process limitation that places the client at risk of financial exploitation

claims.claim: Financial exploitation definition (used in summary)
claims.quote: means the use or control of, or deprivation of the use or control of, a financial asset of an individual by a person through undue influence, unlawful conduct or another wrongful act

claims.claim: Obtain TCP name/contact info and written consent concurrently with KYC
claims.quote: take reasonable steps to obtain from the client the name and contact information of a trusted contact person, and the written consent of the client for the Dealer Member to contact the trusted contact person

claims.claim: Purpose (i): possible financial exploitation
claims.quote: the Dealer Member’s concerns about possible financial exploitation of the client

claims.claim: Purpose (ii): mental capacity
claims.quote: the Dealer Member’s concerns about the client’s mental capacity as it relates to the ability of the client to make decisions involving financial matters

claims.claim: Purpose (iii): legal representative
claims.quote: the name and contact information of a legal representative of the client, if any

claims.claim: Individuals only
claims.quote: Subsection 3202(4) does not apply to a Dealer Member in respect of a client that is not an individual.

claims.claim: Client may name more than one TCP
claims.quote: A client may name more than one TCP on their account.

claims.claim: TCP should not be the client's dealing or advising representative (the RR) on the account
claims.quote: A TCP should not be the client’s dealing representative or advising representative on the account.

claims.claim: A POA attorney may be named as TCP; clients encouraged to pick someone not involved in account decisions
claims.quote: attorney under a POA can be named as a TCP, but clients should be encouraged to select an individual who is not involved in making decisions with respect to the client’s account

claims.claim: TCP acts like an emergency contact; cannot make decisions or account changes

claims.claim: TCP has no authority to transact (does not replace POA)

claims.claim: RDI must describe the circumstances in which the firm might disclose client/account information to the TCP (used in 1.6 and 1.12)
claims.quote: a description of the circumstances under which a Dealer Member might disclose information about the client or the client’s account to a trusted contact person

claims.claim: Refusal: account may be opened, reasonable steps still required

claims.claim: Refusal: may inquire about reasons
claims.quote: the registrant may make further inquiries about the reasons for the refusal

claims.claim: Records demonstrating TCP compliance (NI 31-103 11.5(2)(l))
claims.quote: demonstrate compliance with sections 13.2, 13.2.01, 13.2.1 and 13.3

claims.claim: Ask again at each update
claims.quote: at each update, registrants should ask such clients if they would like to provide the information

claims.claim: Speak to client first before contacting TCP
claims.quote: registrants should speak with the client about concerns they have with the client’s account or wellbeing before contacting others, including the TCP

claims.claim: Contact TCP when client unreachable after repeated attempts
claims.quote: if the registrant is unsuccessful in contacting the client after repeated attempts and where failure to contact the client would be unusual

claims.claim: Do not contact TCP suspected of exploitation; consider police/PGT
claims.quote: If the TCP is suspected of being involved in the financial exploitation of the client, the TCP should not be contacted

claims.claim: Alternative resources: police, public guardian and trustee
claims.quote: such as the police, the public guardian and trustee or an alternative TCP, if named

claims.claim: Exploitation warning sign: sudden withdrawals
claims.quote: unexplained or sudden withdrawals from accounts or account closures
